minutes.headline: Water district and Hickory Hills landowners still split on Zone One control; district to write DEP before any well study.
minutes.summary: The commissioners met two Hickory Hills landowners' board members about the Hickory Hills well and a possible joint study. The debate was over whether the district must own or control Zone One under 310 CMR 22 and what lake-use restrictions could follow. The district agreed to send a letter to DEP, copying the landowners, and to revisit the study scope after a reply. A pump test proposal for a new well was approved by voice vote near the end.

what_happened.line: The Water District and two Hickory Hills landowners' board members stayed split on who must control Zone One around the Hickory Hills well.
The district agreed to send its own letter to DEP after an email vote of the board, copying the landowners; another meeting follows once DEP replies.
The board approved the Well 9 phase two pump test proposal by voice vote; the count was not audible and the caption wording is partly garbled.
A special meeting would be held once the study scope is agreed, rather than waiting for the annual meeting.
Landowners are to mark up concerns on the proposed zone bylaw, with a possible November town meeting article after consulting the hydrogeologist.

why_it_matters: Who controls Zone One around a public well, and what limits follow for lake use, bears on lakefront property owners and on the district's ability to protect a water source and seek grant funding.
If the aquifer protection bylaw goes to a November town meeting, residents would be asked to vote on it.
